questions.question: Which of the following is NOT correct regarding Malwares?

options.text: A Virus infects other programs by modifying them to include a possibly evolved copy of itself.
Worms copy themselves from system to system, rather than infiltrating legitimate files.
Trojans are used to create back-doors on computers belonging to a secure network.
Hoax invades a computer and monitors a user’s activities without consent.

questions.solution:
Option __**4**__ is NOT correct.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Malware:**

 
• Software designed to perform an **unwanted illegal act via the computer network**.
 
• Can be classified **on the basis of execution**:
 
 
• **Virus:** Infects other programs by modifying them to include a possibly evolved copy of itself.
 
• **Worm:** Copy themselves from system to system, rather than infiltrating legitimate files.
 
• **Trojan: **Impairs the security of a system and is used to create back-doors on computers belonging to a secure network.
 
• **Hoax:** It invades the system and deletes an important file when a program is run to correct the harming system.
 
• **Spyware:** Invades a computer and monitors a user’s activities without consent. **So, option 4 is NOT correct**.

questions.question: The time required to move the read/write head to the desired track of a disk is called
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option (3)**

__**Concept:-**__

**Seek time:- **The seek time is the time it takes for the read/write head of the disc to move from one part of the disc to another.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The time it takes a hard disc controller to locate a specific piece of stored data is known as seek time.
 
• The read/write head of the disc must move to the correct location when anything is read or written to it. Seeking refers to the physical placement of the disk's read/write head.
 
• Due to the changing distance between the start point and where the read/write head has been directed to proceed, the seek time for a particular disc might vary.
 
• The average seeks time is commonly used to measure seek time. Track to track and entire stroke are two more ways to quantify seek time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**** Access time:-** It's the time it takes for a computer to request data and then for that request to be fulfilled. Memory, hard drives, CD-ROMs, and other mechanisms are all affected by access time.

**Latency:- **Rotational time is another name for rotational latency. The interval between information requests and the hard disc moving to the right sector is known as the rotational delay.

**Page fault:-** When a software tries to access data or code that is in its address space but not already in the system RAM, a page fault occurs.

questions.question:
Arrange the following types of memory in increasing order based on data transfer rate.

a. HDD

b. SSD

c. RAM

d. Cache memory

e. Registers
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The data transfer rate refers to the speed at which data can be read from or written to a memory device.
 
• Memory devices arranged in increasing order of data transfer rate are **HDD (Hard Disk Drive), SSD (Solid State Drive), RAM (Random Access Memory), Cache Memory, and Registers**.
 
• **HDD:** Slowest among the given options due to mechanical parts and magnetic storage.
 
• **SSD:** Faster than HDD due to the absence of moving parts and reliance on flash storage technology.
 
• **RAM, Cache Memory, and Registers:** Progressively faster due to their proximity to the CPU and design for high-speed data transfer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **HDD (Hard Disk Drive):**

 
 
• Uses spinning magnetic disks to read/write data.
 
• Data transfer rates typically range between 80-160 MB/s.
 
 
 
• **SSD (Solid State Drive):**
 
 
• Utilizes flash memory for data storage, enabling faster access speeds.
 
• Data transfer rates range from 200 MB/s to 3,500 MB/s or more, depending on the interface (SATA, NVMe).
 
 
 
• **RAM (Random Access Memory):**
 
 
• Volatile memory directly accessible by the CPU.
 
• Data transfer rates typically range between 10-25 GB/s for DDR4 RAM.
 
 
 
• **Cache Memory:**
 
 
• A small-sized, high-speed memory located inside or near the CPU.
 
• Used to store frequently accessed data for quick retrieval.
 
 
 
• **Registers:**
 
 
• Smallest and fastest memory directly within the CPU.
 
• Handles data at CPU speed, typically in the range of several GB/s.

questions.question: Which computer virus records every movement you make on your computer?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Key logger**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **keylogger **is a type of **surveillance technology** used to monitor and record each keystroke typed on a specific computer's keyboard.
 
• Keylogger software typically runs in the background, unseen by the user, recording every keystroke made on the computer.
 
• When used maliciously, keyloggers are often secretly installed on a person's device without their knowledge.
 
• The information collected can include sensitive data like usernames, passwords, credit card numbers, and other personal details. This information can then be used for fraudulent activities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

The other options listed are not necessarily associated with recording every movement on a computer:

 
• **DOS **typically refers to Denial of Service, a type of attack designed to overload a network or service, causing it to be unavailable to its intended users.
 
• **Malware Android **refers to malicious software specifically designed to target Android devices. While this can take many forms, it's not necessarily linked to recording every movement.
 
• **Trapper** doesn't match any notable virus category.

questions.question: Which of the following abbreviations represents a volatile memory technology commonly used for the primary working memory in personal computers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**DRAM**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **DRAM (Dynamic Random Access Memory)** is a type of volatile memory that is widely used as the primary working memory (RAM) in personal computers.
 
• It requires constant refreshing of data multiple times per second to retain information, making it "dynamic."
 
• DRAM is faster than traditional storage devices such as hard drives but slower than SRAM (Static Random Access Memory).
 
• It is cost-effective and offers high storage density, which is why it is the preferred choice for system memory in most PCs and laptops.
 
• DRAM modules are available in various forms, such as DDR (Double Data Rate) versions like DDR3, DDR4, and DDR5, which enhance speed and efficiency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Volatile Memory:**

 
 
• Volatile memory requires a constant power supply to retain data. When the power is turned off, all data is lost.
 
• Examples include DRAM and SRAM, used mainly for temporary data storage during system operations.
 
 
 
• **SRAM (Static Random Access Memory):**
 
 
• SRAM is another type of volatile memory that does not require constant refreshing to retain data.
 
• It is faster but more expensive and less dense compared to DRAM, making it suitable for cache memory in CPUs.
 
 
 
• **DDR (Double Data Rate) DRAM:**
 
 
• DDR memory improves the performance of DRAM by transferring data on both the rising and falling edges of the clock signal.
 
• DDR4 and DDR5 are the most commonly used DRAM types in modern computers, offering higher bandwidth and lower power consumption.
 
 
 
• **Non-Volatile Memory:**
 
 
• Non-volatile memory retains data even when the power is turned off, making it ideal for long-term data storage.
 
• Examples include flash memory, SSDs, and ROM (Read-Only Memory).
 
 
 
• **CMOS (Complementary Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor):**
 
 
• CMOS is a low-power semiconductor technology used for constructing integrated circuits.
 
• It is commonly used for small amounts of memory in devices like BIOS to store system settings.

questions.question: While working on a large worksheet, which element should be used to keep the top heading row visible at all times when scrolling down to edit data in lower rows?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Freeze Panes**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Freeze Panes** is an Excel feature used to lock specific rows or columns in place so they remain visible while scrolling through the rest of the worksheet.
 
• This functionality is particularly useful when working on large datasets, ensuring that important headers or labels are always accessible.
 
• To apply Freeze Panes, go to the **View** tab in Excel and select the desired row or column to freeze.
 
• When activated, it divides the worksheet into panes, allowing the frozen section to stay static while other sections can be scrolled through.
 
• This feature improves data visibility, making it easier to analyze or edit information without losing track of key reference points.

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Steps to Use Freeze Panes:**

 
 
• Navigate to the **View** tab in Excel.
 
• Select the row below or the column to the right of the area you want to freeze.
 
• Click on **Freeze Panes** and choose from the options: **Freeze Panes, Freeze Top Row, or Freeze First Column**.
 
 
 
• **Benefits of Freeze Panes:**
 
 
• Enhances readability of large spreadsheets by keeping headers or labels in view.
 
• Facilitates easier navigation and data entry without losing track of reference points.
 
 
 
• **Limitations:**
 
 
• Freeze Panes works only within the same worksheet and cannot be applied across multiple sheets.
 
• It may not be suitable for smaller datasets where all rows and columns are already visible.
